questions.question: Before leaving a bus stop, a driver should:

options.text: Check that no students are running to catch the bus.
Check that students have put their backpacks in the aisle.
Check that students have opened the emergency vent.
Check that students are facing the back of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that no students are running to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: Before driving away from a bus stop, always check that no students are running to catch the bus.

questions.question: What should properly adjusted outside side flat mirrors on a school bus allow the driver to see?

options.text: The sides of the school bus
Under the school bus
The front tires touching the ground
Vehicles in front of the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the school bus
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted outside side mirrors let you see along the sides of the bus, the rear tires touching the ground, and 200 feet behind the bus.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, you need to identify all of the following, except:

options.text: The power steering belt.
The water pump belt.
The alternator belt.
The water compressor belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water compressor belt.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, you must check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt. Check them for cracks, frays, and tightness. If any of these parts are not belt-driven, tell the examiner and verify they are working properly, mounted securely, and not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: If you miss a student's stop while bringing students home after school, you should:

options.text: Back up to the stop.
Follow the procedures your school district has set up.
Not worry about the student.
Stop quickly and let them exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the procedures your school district has set up.
questions.explanation: If you forget to stop where a student needs to get off, do not back up. Instead, follow your school district's established procedures.

questions.question: Students should board a school bus:

options.text: In a single line, one after another.
Two at a time.
In as large a group as possible.
However they want. It makes no difference.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single line, one after another.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single line while holding the handrails.

questions.question: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, you should:

options.text: Back up before any students board the bus.
Let all students board the bus first, then back up.
Let half the students board, then back up toward the rest.
Tell students to wait at the stop, then back toward them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let all students board the bus first, then back up.
questions.explanation: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, pick up all students before backing up. Watch carefully for late arrivals when backing.

questions.question: If a student drops an item while walking to the bus, the student should:

options.text: Stop and pick up the object.
Have another student pick it up.
Ask the driver to pick up the object.
Leave the item and walk away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask the driver to pick up the object.
questions.explanation: Students should not pick up dropped items because they could move out of the driver's sight at a dangerous moment. If something is dropped, the student should move away from the bus's danger zone, get the driver's attention, and ask the driver to retrieve it.

questions.question: When asked to do a parallel parking maneuver on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: You may need to parallel park into a space on the left side of your vehicle. Drive past the space first, then back into it. Bring the rear of your vehicle as close to the rear of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely within the space's boundaries.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check traffic first.
Not use your mirrors.
Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow the instructions.
Not make the lane change if you don't want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic first.
questions.explanation: You will be asked to change lanes during the driving skills test. Always check traffic first and use proper signals before changing lanes. Change lanes smoothly when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Points are taken away for each pull-up.
A driver is allowed three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up only counts if the driver gets out of the vehicle first.
Too many pull-ups will be counted as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too many pull-ups will be counted as errors.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, you do not lose points for one pull-up. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located on a school bus?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side
Above the door on the passenger side
Above the emergency door in the rear
Under the driver's seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. It lets the driver see what students are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: What is the inside rearview mirror of a school bus used for?

options.text: Watch passengers.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.
See in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror on a school bus is used to watch what passengers are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/left parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Go straight forward, then back to the right.
Go straight forward, then back to the left.
Go forward to the right, then back straight.
Go forward to the left, then back straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, go straight forward first, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space lines.

questions.question: What do crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see?

options.text: The front bumper danger zones.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.
Vehicles in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper danger zones.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help drivers see the danger zones in front of the bus and on both sides of the bus. These zones stretch from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, what should you check about emergency exits?

options.text: That they are hard to open.
That the warning devices work.
That they squeak.
That they cannot be reached from inside the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the warning devices work.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits should open smoothly, have no damage, and close securely from the inside.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Ensure the fluid level is above the full mark.
Ensure the fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure the fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, you must show where the dipstick is, check that there is enough power steering fluid, and ensure the level is above the refill mark. It does not need to be above the full mark.

questions.question: When should outside mirrors on a school bus be adjusted?

options.text: Before the trip starts.
During the trip.
After students board.
After the trip ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip starts.
questions.explanation: All mirrors should be checked and adjusted before starting a trip. Good mirror adjustment keeps all students and nearby vehicles safe.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before turning, what should you do?

options.text: Skid to a stop.
Stop past the stop line for a better view.
Let your vehicle roll.
Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the front wheels pointed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind the stop line or crosswalk with your front wheels pointed straight. Do not let the vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can still see its rear tires.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection, which is NOT required about engine oil?

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show the oil level is safe.
Show the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, you must show where the dipstick is, prove the oil level is safe, and show it is above the refill mark. It should never be below the refill mark.

questions.question: What is true about loading and unloading a school bus?

options.text: It can be dangerous for passengers.
It does not need to be watched.
It should happen while refueling.
The driver can talk to other drivers while doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be dangerous for passengers.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. School bus drivers must follow safety rules and watch carefully during these times.
